check.weakExistence: {name} depends on its owner by existence only (E); a weak entity is usually identified through it (I, or an identifying relation).
check.weakIdentifying: {name} is weak, but no identifying relation joins it to its owner.
check.weakPartialKey: {name} is weak and has no partial key (~name).
check.weakTotal: {entity} should take part (1,1) in {relation}, its identifying relation.
check.partialKeyStrong: {name} is a partial key, but {entity} isn't weak.
check.alternateKeyDerived: {name} is an alternate key but derived.
check.alternateKeyMultivalued: {name} is an alternate key but multivalued.
check.relationDependency: {name} has both the I and the E mark; a dependency is by identification or by existence.
check.relationRoles: {name} relates {entity} to itself; give each side a role.
check.associativeKey: {name} is an associative entity without a key attribute.
check.relationConvert: {name} relates {count} sides; Convert to entity turns it into an entity with a two-way relation per side.
check.relationAllOne: Every side of {name} is at most one; a relation of three or more is usually many on some side.
check.isaNoChildren: The hierarchy under {parent} has no children; it usually has two or more.
check.isaOneChild: The hierarchy under {parent} has one child; it usually has two or more.
check.unionNoSuperclasses: The union type of {category} has no superclasses; it unites two or more.
check.unionOneSuperclass: The union type of {category} has one superclass; it unites two or more.

standard.label: Standard
standard.missing: This standard isn't installed (a plugin that was removed?), so the diagram is drawn with the default.
standard.approximate: Drawn from secondary sources: check the book for its exact symbols, and adjust the settings below if they differ.

standards.cloudy: (min,max) on the lines, the ratio on the diamond, triangle hierarchies and crow's feet.
standards.chen: The original model: 1, N and M on the lines; no hierarchies, aggregations or constraints.
standards.elmasri: 1 / N on the lines, double lines for total participation, the d / o circle.
standards.silberschatz: Cardinality limits on the lines, double lines for total participation, aggregation.
standards.piattini: (min,max) on the lines, the ratio on the diamond, triangle hierarchies, aggregation and constraints.
standards.cloudyCitation: The board's own mix of the common notations.

cardinality.label: Cardinality on the lines
cardinality.hint: What each line says about its side.

arrows.label: Arrowheads
arrows.hint: On two-way relations, at an entity the other side takes part with at most once.

joins.label: Join attributes
joins.hint: The attribute a relation joins through, after the cardinality.

dependency.label: Dependency marks
dependency.hint: The I (identification) and E (existence) marks on relations.

crowFeet.label: Crow's feet
crowFeet.hint: Marks where two-way relations meet entities.

aggregate.name: Aggregation name

attribute.name: Attribute name
attribute.partialTitle: Partial key of a weak entity (dashed underline)
attribute.optionalTitle: Optional (half-filled circle in the lollipop style)

constraint.exclusiveHint: The entity takes part in only one of the two relations.
constraint.inclusiveHint: To take part in the second, the entity must take part in the first (min,max) times.
constraint.exclusionHint: The same occurrences can't be in both relations.
constraint.inclusionHint: Occurrences of the second relation must exist in the first.

entity.specialize: Specialize this entity into child entities (ES UN)

relation.name: Relation name

union.intro: Each {name} is exactly one of the superclasses below (a category).
union.addExisting: Add an existing entity as a superclass

toTables.title: Create tables from {label}
toTables.description: Each entity, multivalued attribute and many-to-many relation becomes a table, and the other relations foreign keys. Tables that already exist with the same names are updated.
toTables.perEntityHint: Children keyed by the parent's key.
toTables.singleHint: Every column in the parent's table, with a discriminator.
toTables.warnNeedsSides: {name} needs two sides with tables, so it was left out.
toTables.warnConstraints: Constraints between relations have no tables; enforce them in the application.
toTables.warnGuessed: Column types were guessed from their names; check them in the database panel.
toTables.warnNoKey: {name} has no key, so it got an id column.
toTables.warnLoop: {name}'s owners form a loop, so it's keyed like a strong entity.
toTables.warnNoPartial: {name} is weak but has no partial key; its key is its owner's.
toTables.warnDerived: {name} is derived, so it has no column.
